description: Original multiple-choice questions for CBSE Class 10 (India) in Mathematics, Science and Social Science, written to the chapters of the current rationalised NCERT textbooks.

curricula.name: CBSE
curricula.description: Central Board of Secondary Education: a national school board in India whose affiliated schools teach from NCERT textbooks and follow the CBSE curriculum.

levels.name: Class 10
levels.description: The final year of secondary school, ending in the CBSE Class X board examination. Topics follow the rationalised NCERT textbooks prescribed by the CBSE secondary curriculum for 2025–26.

topics.name: Real Numbers
topics.description: The Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic, HCF and LCM by prime factorisation, and proofs that numbers such as √2 are irrational.

topics.name: Polynomials
topics.description: Zeroes of a polynomial, their graphical meaning, and the relationship between the zeroes and coefficients of a quadratic polynomial.

topics.name: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
topics.description: Graphical solution, consistency and number of solutions, and solving by substitution and elimination.

topics.name: Quadratic Equations
topics.description: Standard form, solving by factorisation and the quadratic formula, and the discriminant and nature of roots.

topics.name: Arithmetic Progressions
topics.description: The nth term of an AP and the sum of its first n terms, applied to everyday problems.

topics.name: Triangles
topics.description: Similar triangles, the Basic Proportionality Theorem and its converse, and the AAA, SSS and SAS similarity criteria.

topics.name: Coordinate Geometry
topics.description: The distance formula and the section formula for internal division.

topics.name: Introduction to Trigonometry
topics.description: Trigonometric ratios of acute angles, values at 0°, 30°, 45°, 60° and 90°, and simple identities from sin²A + cos²A = 1.

topics.name: Some Applications of Trigonometry
topics.description: Heights and distances using angles of elevation and depression of 30°, 45° and 60°.

topics.name: Circles
topics.description: Tangents to a circle: the tangent is perpendicular to the radius, and tangents from an external point are equal.

topics.name: Areas Related to Circles
topics.description: Areas of sectors and segments of a circle and lengths of arcs.

topics.name: Surface Areas and Volumes
topics.description: Surface areas and volumes of solids made by combining two of cubes, cuboids, cylinders, cones, spheres and hemispheres.

topics.name: Statistics
topics.description: Mean, median and mode of grouped data.

topics.name: Probability
topics.description: Classical (theoretical) probability of simple events.

topics.name: Chemical Reactions and Equations
topics.description: Balanced equations; combination, decomposition, displacement and double displacement reactions; oxidation and reduction.

topics.name: Acids, Bases and Salts
topics.description: Indicators, reactions of acids and bases, the pH scale and its importance, and common salts such as baking soda and bleaching powder.

topics.name: Metals and Non-metals
topics.description: Properties of metals and non-metals, the reactivity series, ionic compounds, basic metallurgy and corrosion.

topics.name: Carbon and its Compounds
topics.description: Covalent bonding, hydrocarbons, homologous series, functional groups, ethanol, ethanoic acid, and soaps and detergents.

topics.name: Life Processes
topics.description: Nutrition, respiration, transportation and excretion in plants and animals.

topics.name: Control and Coordination
topics.description: The nervous system and reflex actions, plant movements and hormones, and the animal endocrine system.

topics.name: How do Organisms Reproduce?
topics.description: Asexual and sexual reproduction in plants and animals, and reproductive health.

topics.name: Heredity
topics.description: Variation, Mendel's experiments and the rules of inheritance, and sex determination.

topics.name: Light – Reflection and Refraction
topics.description: Spherical mirrors and lenses, image formation, the mirror and lens formulae, refractive index and power of a lens.

topics.name: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
topics.description: The eye, defects of vision and their correction, dispersion through a prism and scattering of light.

topics.name: Electricity
topics.description: Current, potential difference, Ohm's law, resistance and resistivity, series and parallel resistors, heating effect and electric power.

topics.name: Magnetic Effects of Electric Current
topics.description: Magnetic field lines, fields of wires, coils and solenoids, force on a current-carrying conductor, and domestic circuits.

topics.name: Our Environment
topics.description: Ecosystems, food chains and the flow of energy, ozone depletion, and biodegradable and non-biodegradable waste.

topics.name: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe
topics.description: History: the French Revolution and the idea of the nation, liberal nationalism, the revolutions of 1848, and the making of Germany and Italy.

topics.name: Nationalism in India
topics.description: History: the First World War, Khilafat and Non-Cooperation, Civil Disobedience, and the sense of collective belonging.

topics.name: Resources and Development
topics.description: Geography: types of resources, resource planning, land use, and the soils of India and their conservation.

topics.name: Water Resources
topics.description: Geography: water scarcity, multipurpose river projects, and rainwater harvesting.

topics.name: Agriculture
topics.description: Geography: types of farming, cropping seasons, major crops and where they grow.

topics.name: Power Sharing
topics.description: Political Science: the cases of Belgium and Sri Lanka, why power sharing is desirable, and its forms.

topics.name: Federalism
topics.description: Political Science: features of federalism, the Union, State and Concurrent Lists, and decentralisation in India.

topics.name: Political Parties
topics.description: Political Science: what parties do, party systems, national and state parties, and challenges to parties.

topics.name: Development
topics.description: Economics: development goals, comparing countries by income, per capita income, and human development indicators.

topics.name: Sectors of the Indian Economy
topics.description: Economics: primary, secondary and tertiary sectors, organised and unorganised sectors, public and private sectors, and employment.

topics.name: Money and Credit
topics.description: Economics: money as a medium of exchange, banks, terms of credit, formal and informal credit, and self-help groups.

questions.prompt: The HCF of two numbers is 6 and their LCM is 180. If one of the numbers is 30, what is the other?
questions.explanation: HCF × LCM = product of the two numbers, so the other number = (6 × 180) ÷ 30 = 1080 ÷ 30 = 36. Check: HCF(30, 36) = 6 and LCM(30, 36) = 180.

questions.prompt: Which of these numbers is irrational?
questions.explanation: √5 is irrational, and a rational number plus an irrational number is irrational. √49 = 7, 22/7 is a fraction and 0.333… = 1/3, so those three are rational.

questions.prompt: What is the sum of the zeroes of the polynomial 2x² − 8x + 5?
questions.explanation: For ax² + bx + c, the sum of the zeroes is −b/a = −(−8)/2 = 4. (5/2 is c/a, which is the product of the zeroes.)

questions.prompt: How many solutions does the pair of equations 2x + 3y = 5 and 4x + 6y = 7 have?
questions.explanation: a₁/a₂ = 2/4 = 1/2 and b₁/b₂ = 3/6 = 1/2, but c₁/c₂ = 5/7. Equal x and y ratios with a different constant ratio means the lines are parallel, so there is no solution.

source.reference: Chapter 3, Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables

questions.prompt: What is the nature of the roots of x² − 6x + 9 = 0?

options.text: One positive root and one negative root

questions.explanation: The discriminant b² − 4ac = 36 − 36 = 0, so the roots are real and equal (both are 3).

questions.prompt: For what positive value of k does x² + kx + 16 = 0 have two equal roots?
questions.explanation: Equal roots need b² − 4ac = 0: k² − 4 × 1 × 16 = 0, so k² = 64 and k = 8 (taking the positive value).

questions.prompt: What is the 10th term of the AP 3, 7, 11, 15, …?
questions.explanation: Here a = 3 and d = 4, so aₙ = a + (n − 1)d gives a₁₀ = 3 + 9 × 4 = 39. (43 comes from using n instead of n − 1.)

questions.prompt: The sum of the first n terms of an AP is n² + 2n. What is its 10th term?
questions.explanation: a₁₀ = S₁₀ − S₉ = (100 + 20) − (81 + 18) = 120 − 99 = 21. (120 is the sum of the first 10 terms, not the 10th term.)

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, DE ∥ BC with D on AB and E on AC. If AD = 2 cm, DB = 3 cm and AE = 4 cm, what is EC?
questions.explanation: By the Basic Proportionality Theorem, AD/DB = AE/EC, so 2/3 = 4/EC and EC = 6 cm. (10 cm is the whole of AC.)

questions.prompt: What is the distance between the points (1, 2) and (4, 6)?
Which point divides the line segment joining A(1, 3) and B(7, 9) internally in the ratio 1 : 2?
questions.explanation: Section formula: ((1 × 7 + 2 × 1)/3, (1 × 9 + 2 × 3)/3) = (9/3, 15/3) = (3, 5), one third of the way from A. (5, 7) uses the ratio 2 : 1 and (4, 6) is the midpoint.

questions.prompt: If tan A = 5/12 and A is an acute angle, what is sin A?
questions.explanation: Take opposite side 5 and adjacent side 12; the hypotenuse is √(25 + 144) = 13. So sin A = opposite/hypotenuse = 5/13. (12/13 is cos A.)

questions.prompt: A vertical flagpole casts a shadow 20 m long on level ground when the sun's angle of elevation is 60°. How tall is the flagpole?
questions.explanation: tan 60° = height ÷ shadow length, so height = 20 × √3 = 20√3 m (about 34.6 m). 20/√3 m comes from using tan 30° by mistake; 40 m is the distance from the shadow's tip to the top of the pole.

questions.prompt: A tangent is drawn from a point P to a circle of radius 8 cm. If P is 17 cm from the centre, how long is the tangent from P?
questions.explanation: The tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact, so tangent² = 17² − 8² = 289 − 64 = 225, giving 15 cm.

questions.prompt: What is the area of a sector of a circle of radius 9 cm whose central angle is 40°?
questions.explanation: Area = (θ/360°) × πr² = (40/360) × π × 81 = 9π cm². 81π cm² is the whole circle, and 2π cm is the length of this sector's arc, not its area.

questions.prompt: A solid is a cylinder of radius r and height h with a hemisphere of the same radius fixed on top. What is its volume?
questions.explanation: Add the parts: the cylinder is πr²h and the hemisphere is half of (4/3)πr³, which is (2/3)πr³. (4/3)πr³ is a whole sphere and (1/3)πr²h is a cone.

questions.prompt: In grouped data the modal class is 20–30 with frequency 12. The class before it has frequency 8 and the class after it has 6. What is the mode?
A fair die is thrown once. What is the probability of getting a perfect square?
questions.explanation: 1 = 1² and 4 = 2² are the perfect squares on a die: 2 of the 6 equally likely outcomes, so P = 2/6 = 1/3. (Forgetting that 1 is a perfect square gives 1/6.)

questions.prompt: Quicklime reacts with water: CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂. What type of reaction is this?
questions.explanation: Two substances join to form a single product, so it is a combination reaction (it also gives out heat). Decomposition is the reverse: one substance breaking into two or more.

questions.prompt: In the reaction CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O, which substance is oxidised?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen gains oxygen to become water, so H₂ is oxidised. Copper(II) oxide loses oxygen, so it is reduced; Cu and H₂O are the products.

questions.prompt: A solution turns red litmus paper blue. Which pH could it have?
questions.explanation: Turning red litmus blue shows the solution is basic, and basic solutions have a pH above 7. pH 7 is neutral; pH 1 and 4 are acidic.

questions.prompt: Which gas is given off when zinc granules are warmed with sodium hydroxide solution?
questions.explanation: Zinc reacts with sodium hydroxide to form sodium zincate and hydrogen gas: 2NaOH + Zn → Na₂ZnO₂ + H₂.

questions.prompt: Which of these metals does NOT give hydrogen gas with dilute hydrochloric acid?
questions.explanation: Only metals above hydrogen in the activity series displace hydrogen from dilute acids. Copper is below hydrogen; magnesium, zinc and iron are above it.

questions.prompt: Which of these could be the molecular formula of an alkyne?
questions.explanation: Alkynes have a triple bond and fit CₙH₂ₙ₋₂; for n = 3 that is C₃H₄ (propyne). C₃H₈ fits the alkane formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, and C₃H₆ and C₄H₈ fit the alkene formula CₙH₂ₙ.

questions.prompt: In aerobic respiration, where in the cell is pyruvate broken down using oxygen?
questions.explanation: Glucose is first split into pyruvate in the cytoplasm. The breakdown of pyruvate using oxygen, into carbon dioxide and water, happens in the mitochondria.

questions.prompt: What are the tiny filtering units of the human kidney called?
questions.explanation: Each kidney has a large number of nephrons that filter the blood. Neurons are nerve cells, alveoli are air sacs in the lungs and villi line the small intestine.

questions.prompt: Which plant hormone inhibits growth and causes wilting of leaves?
questions.explanation: Abscisic acid is a growth inhibitor; its effects include wilting of leaves. Auxins, gibberellins and cytokinins all promote growth.

questions.prompt: In a flowering plant, what does the ovary develop into after fertilisation?
questions.explanation: After fertilisation the ovary grows and ripens into the fruit. The ovule becomes the seed, and the zygote inside it grows into the embryo.

questions.prompt: Pea plants with round yellow seeds (RRYY) are crossed with wrinkled green ones (rryy), and the F1 are self-crossed. What fraction of the F2 is wrinkled and green?
questions.explanation: The F1 is RrYy. Wrinkled needs rr (1/4) and green needs yy (1/4), inherited independently, so 1/4 × 1/4 = 1/16. The F2 ratio is 9 round yellow : 3 round green : 3 wrinkled yellow : 1 wrinkled green.

questions.prompt: In the food chain grass → deer → lion, the grass holds 10,000 J of energy. By the 10% rule, about how much energy reaches the lion?
questions.explanation: About 10% passes to each next level: 10,000 J × 10% = 1,000 J reaches the deer, then 1,000 J × 10% = 100 J reaches the lion.

questions.prompt: The centre of curvature of a concave mirror is 24 cm in front of its pole. How far from the pole is its principal focus?
questions.explanation: The principal focus lies midway between the pole and the centre of curvature, so f = R/2 = 24/2 = 12 cm.

questions.prompt: An object is placed 30 cm from a convex lens of focal length 15 cm. What kind of image is formed?

options.text: Real, inverted and the same size

questions.explanation: 30 cm is twice the focal length, so the object is at 2F. The image forms at 2F on the other side of the lens: real, inverted and the same size as the object.

questions.prompt: Rahul sees his phone screen clearly, but distant road signs look blurred. Which defect of vision does he have, and which lens corrects it?
questions.explanation: Seeing near objects clearly but not distant ones is myopia (near-sightedness). A concave (diverging) lens of suitable power corrects it.

source.reference: Chapter 10, The Human Eye and the Colourful World

questions.prompt: Two 6 Ω resistors are connected in parallel. What is their equivalent resistance?
questions.explanation: 1/R = 1/6 + 1/6 = 2/6 = 1/3, so R = 3 Ω. 12 Ω is the series value, and 1/3 is the value of 1/R, not R.

questions.prompt: A wire of resistance R is stretched to twice its length while its volume stays the same. What is its new resistance?
questions.explanation: R = ρl/A. Doubling the length at constant volume halves the cross-sectional area, so the new resistance is ρ(2l)/(A/2) = 4ρl/A = 4R.

questions.prompt: What do the magnetic field lines inside a long current-carrying solenoid look like?

options.text: Lines spreading out from the centre
There are no field lines inside

questions.explanation: Inside a long solenoid the field lines are parallel straight lines, showing the field is uniform there. Concentric circles are the pattern around a straight current-carrying wire.

source.reference: Chapter 12, Magnetic Effects of Electric Current

questions.prompt: Who is described as the architect of German unification, carried out with the help of the Prussian army and bureaucracy?
questions.explanation: Otto von Bismarck, chief minister of Prussia, led German unification through wars with Denmark, Austria and France. William I was proclaimed emperor in 1871; Mazzini and Cavour belong to Italy's story.

source.reference: India and the Contemporary World II, Chapter 1, The Rise of Nationalism in Europe

questions.prompt: Which country was recognised as an independent nation by the Treaty of Constantinople of 1832?
questions.explanation: Greece, part of the Ottoman Empire since the fifteenth century, began its struggle for independence in 1821 and was recognised as independent by the Treaty of Constantinople in 1832.

source.reference: India and the Contemporary World II, Chapter 1, The Rise of Nationalism in Europe

questions.prompt: Why did Gandhiji call off the Non-Cooperation Movement in February 1922?

options.text: The Gandhi–Irwin Pact had been signed
The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place
Violence broke out at Chauri Chaura

questions.explanation: At Chauri Chaura (Gorakhpur) a peaceful demonstration turned into a violent clash with the police, so Gandhiji halted the movement. Jallianwala Bagh was in 1919; the Simon Commission (1928) and Gandhi–Irwin Pact (1931) came later.

source.reference: India and the Contemporary World II, Chapter 2, Nationalism in India

questions.prompt: Which soil, also called regur, is ideal for growing cotton?
questions.explanation: Black soil is known as regur soil, and because it suits cotton so well it is also called black cotton soil.

source.reference: Contemporary India II, Chapter 1, Resources and Development

questions.prompt: Which of these is a rabi crop, sown in winter and harvested in summer?
questions.explanation: Rabi crops are sown from October to December and harvested from April to June; wheat, barley, peas, gram and mustard are examples. Paddy, cotton and groundnut are kharif crops, grown with the monsoon.

questions.prompt: In Bikaner, Phalodi and Barmer in Rajasthan, houses traditionally stored rooftop rainwater for drinking in underground tanks. What were these tanks called?
questions.explanation: Tankas were underground tanks, part of rooftop rainwater harvesting, that held drinking water until the next rain. Khadins and johads are rain-fed field storage; kuls are Himalayan diversion channels.

source.reference: Contemporary India II, Chapter 3, Water Resources

questions.prompt: Belgium's 'community government' is elected by the people of one language community, wherever they live. This is power shared among…
questions.explanation: Community government gives each language group (Dutch, French and German speakers) power over cultural, educational and language issues, so it shares power among social groups.

source.reference: Democratic Politics II, Chapter 1, Power Sharing

questions.prompt: In India's Constitution, which list contains subjects such as defence, foreign affairs and banking?
questions.explanation: Subjects of national importance, such as defence, foreign affairs, banking, communications and currency, are in the Union List, and only the Union Government can make laws on them.

questions.prompt: Every political party in India has to register with which body?
questions.explanation: Parties register with the Election Commission of India, which also recognises large, established parties and gives them a unique election symbol.

source.reference: Democratic Politics II, Chapter 4, Political Parties

questions.prompt: Which organisation publishes the Human Development Report, which compares countries by education, health and per capita income?
questions.explanation: The Human Development Report is published by the UNDP (United Nations Development Programme). The World Bank, by contrast, compares countries mainly by per capita income.

questions.prompt: As the NCERT textbook describes it, how many days of work a year did MGNREGA 2005 guarantee to people in rural areas who needed work?
questions.explanation: MGNREGA 2005 guaranteed 100 days of employment a year to rural people able and needing to work, or an unemployment allowance. (In 2025 a new Act, VB-G RAM G, replaced it with 125 days from July 2026.)

source.reference: Understanding Economic Development, Chapter 2, Sectors of the Indian Economy

questions.prompt: A farmer borrows money to grow a crop, pests destroy the crop, and he must sell part of his land to repay the loan. What is this situation called?
questions.explanation: When credit leaves the borrower worse off and recovery is very painful, as here, it is called a debt trap. Collateral is an asset pledged against a loan; terms of credit are the loan's conditions.

source.reference: Understanding Economic Development, Chapter 3, Money and Credit
